check.title: Then it checks the work
check.sub: Before anything goes live, Brand Check reviews it against {name}'s guidelines, flags potential issues, and shows which guideline informed each finding.
check.note: Brand Check runs on the context you already keep in Frontify. It's more than a prompt: it's a service built into Frontify, available in the portal and through the API. The image is fictional AI-generated work content, and the findings are samples.

asset.by: fictional, made with a generic AI image tool
asset.alt: A fictional AI-generated LinkedIn graphic: posed store associates, a coral-orange color wash and a generic headline

findings.text: The coral-orange wash is close to FND red, but it isn't in the palette, and the brand doesn't wash photos.
findings.recommendation: Use FND red, #EA1722, as the action color on white and black, with no color wash over photos.

findings.text: "Elevate Every Room" is a generic line. It names no product or material, so it isn't approved NatureMatch messaging.
findings.recommendation: Start from the approved positioning and name the product and material.

findings.text: A posed group smiling at the camera doesn't match the photography style.
findings.recommendation: Use a candid photo of a real team at work from the photo library.

items.label: Brand
items.title: Our palette
items.rule: FND red is the action color. Layouts stay black and white.
items.ask: Which color should a social post lead with?
items.answer: Use **FND red, #EA1722**. FND red is the action color.

items.label: Creative
items.title: Photography
items.lead: Real teams doing real work, never staged.

do.label: Teams at work
do.note: Candid moments of people working together.

dont.label: Posed for the camera
dont.note: No staged handshakes or stock smiles.

items.ask: Can I use a stock photo of a handshake?
items.answer: Better not. The photography guidelines ask for **candid teamwork**, and **no staged handshakes or stock smiles**.

items.label: Everyday
items.desc: Short rules for email, decks and docs
items.title: Email tone of voice
items.lead: The short version of our tone of voice, for everyone who sends email.
rules: Say what you need in under eight words.
Lead with the ask or the answer.
Use the standard signature. No quotes or images.
items.do: Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?
items.dont: Just circling back on the below!!
items.askLabel: Before sending, in Outlook with Copilot
items.ask: Check this email against our writing guidelines.
items.answer: Two fixes before you send: **put the ask in the first line**, and **use the standard signature**.
items.from: Condensed from Brand › Tone of voice

everyday.eyebrow: Use case 5 · Everyday guidelines, inside your office applications
everyday.title: The right tone in every email and deck
everyday.sub: Most of {name} will never open a brand portal. With Frontify connected, Claude inside your email and presentation apps reads the Everyday guidelines and checks the work before it goes out.
everyday.note: Claude for Microsoft 365 reads Frontify through the Frontify connector (MCP) once it's set up in your Claude workspace. Sample email, deck and guidelines.

tabs.label: Email
tabs.ask: Check this email against our email tone of voice before I send it.
tabs.intro: Three fixes based on **Everyday › Email tone of voice**:

before.subject: Following up
body: Hi team, just circling back on the below!!
We've been heads-down on the NatureMatch launch and there's a lot going on, so I wanted to share where things stand.
Can you review the launch plan by Thursday?

after.subject: Review the NatureMatch launch plan by Thursday
body: Hi team, can you review the NatureMatch launch plan by Thursday?
It covers the messaging, launch assets and timeline. Comments in the doc are perfect.

fixes.label: Subject:
fixes.note: say what you need. "Following up" doesn't.

fixes.label: Opening:
fixes.note: lead with the ask. It's in the last line right now.

fixes.label: Sign-off:
fixes.note: use the standard signature, with no quotes.

tabs.done: Updated. The draft matches the email tone of voice and is ready to send.

partners.eyebrow: Use case 6 · Supplier and agency files
partners.title: Supplier and agency files land in the right place
partners.sub: Suppliers and agencies submit packaging artwork straight into {name}'s portal. Files land in the right library, and the assistant tags them and sets an expiry date in one sentence.
partners.note: Sample files, supplier and library. The assistant acts on the assets you select: workflow status, metadata, tags and expiry dates.
partners.ask: Tag these NatureMatch and Packaging artwork, and set them to expire Dec 31, 2026.
partners.plan: I'll add the tags NatureMatch and Packaging artwork, and set Available until to Dec 31, 2026, on the 2 selected assets. Say yes and I'll apply it.
partners.you: You're the packaging supplier. Then see what the brand team gets.

packaging.title: Find every package, and the rules behind it
packaging.sub: {name}'s exclusive-brand packaging lives in one library instead of scattered folders. Search or filter by brand, product line, format, size or logo version, then open any product to see its packaging guideline: every zone on the carton, the rule behind it and the source files.
packaging.note: Sample packages, products, sizes and rules built for this page. Not {name}'s own packaging or guidelines.
packaging.placeholder: Search packaging, e.g. NuCore or laminate
packaging.askLabel: A packaging designer asks the brand assistant

quick.label: Every package with the previous logo

plank.logo: Brand band on the left third of the long face. Current logo only: replace previous-logo cartons at the next print run.
plank.name: Collection and color name, two lines at most, in the brand typeface.
plank.claim: One claim, and it names the material, for example waterproof vinyl plank.
plank.size: Square feet per carton and plank count, bottom right, readable on a pallet.
plank.info: End panel: SKU, barcode, install and care icons, and compliance marks such as CARB where they apply.

box.logo: Brand band across the top of the face. Current logo only.
box.name: Collection and color name, centered, two lines at most.
box.claim: One claim, and it names the material, for example porcelain tile.
box.size: Square feet per carton and piece count, bottom center.
box.info: Side panel: SKU, barcode, tile size, shade and lot, and care icons.

libraryQa.ask: Which packages still use the previous logo?
libraryQa.answer: **5 packages** across NuCore, AquaGuard, DuraLux, Hampstead and Eco Forest. I filtered Packaging by **Logo version: Previous logo**. Open any of them for its dieline and print files.

detailQa.ask: What has to be on the {name} carton?
detailQa.answer: **Brand band, collection name, one material claim and square feet per carton** on the face, with SKU, barcode and care icons on the end panel.
